I haven't run anything. This is route R3 from the fleet skill (laptop WSL → desktop Windows). It goes through the desktop's WSL sshd (`desk-wsl`, port 2222) and then runs `claude.exe` on the Windows side.

**1. Check that the hop works and Windows is signed in:**

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'hostname && cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe -p "echo ok" < /dev/null'
```

You should see `desk-01` and then `ok`. If you get an expired-login error instead, the connection worked but Windows on the desktop is signed out. The last time this route was tested, it reported `loggedIn: false`. Someone has to run `/login` at the desktop's console or over RDP; it can't be fixed remotely.

**2. Start the session:**

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe --bg --name desk-win-inbox "You are a standing receiver on the desk-01 Windows lane. Act on each message other sessions send you and reply to the sender. Do not exit; stop only when a message says STOP." < /dev/null'
```

**3. Confirm it's running:**

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe agents --json --all < /dev/null'
```

**4. Send it a message from any session:**

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe -p "SendMessage to desk-win-inbox: <text>" < /dev/null'
```

Your laptop session can't message it directly. Each lane has its own account, so every message has to go through a turn started on the desktop's Windows side, as in step 4. A session on the desktop's Windows side can message it by name without that.

**Things to check:**
- **The scratch folder must be trusted.** Background sessions only start in a trusted folder; otherwise you get a "workspace not trusted" error. If that happens, run `claude.exe` once in `%USERPROFILE%\scratch` at the desktop and accept the trust prompt.
- **This exact setup hasn't been tested.** Background sessions were only tested on WSL. On Windows started over ssh, it may stop when the ssh connection closes, so run step 3 again after a minute. If it has stopped, the fallback is a `-p -n desk-win-inbox --settings "{\"crossSessionInbound\":\"accept\"}"` receiver run under `nohup … &`. That one only stays up while its turn stays open.
- **The fleet file was generated for desk-01, not lap-01.** I took the `desk-wsl` alias from it. Make sure your laptop's `~/.ssh/config` has that alias, or step 1 will fail.
- **Each message costs usage.** Every step except starting the session runs a new Claude turn on the desktop, and each turn counts against the desktop Windows account.
- **Message text is visible.** It's passed on the command line, which shows in the desktop's process list, so don't put secrets in it. If your text has an apostrophe, write it as `'\''`.

The desktop's Windows side is route R3: from the laptop's WSL, ssh into the desktop's WSL (port 2222), then run the Windows `claude.exe` from there. For a session that stays up and takes messages, start it as a background session (`--bg`). A plain `-p` receiver stops when its single turn ends.

**1. Check the hop first.** This confirms you reach desk-01 and that the desktop's Windows Claude is signed in. The last test of this route found it signed out.

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'hostname && cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe -p "echo ok" < /dev/null'
```

You should see `desk-01` and then `ok`. If you get an expired-OAuth/login error instead, the route worked but someone needs to run `/login` at the desktop's console or over RDP. You can't fix that remotely.

**2. Start the session:**

```sh
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe --bg --name desk-win-inbox "You are a standing message receiver on the desk-01 Windows lane. Stay idle until messages arrive from other sessions. Act on each message as its own task and reply with the result. Stop and report if a message asks for anything destructive or needs a credential." < /dev/null'
```

**Later, to message it or check on it** (each of these starts a new turn on the desktop's Windows side):

```sh
# send a message
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe -p "SendMessage to desk-win-inbox: <text>" < /dev/null'

# check status / get its id
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe agents --json --all'
```

To read its replies, run `--resume <id>` with the id from that list. Don't use `logs`, which prints raw terminal output.

**Things to check:**
- **The desktop has to trust the scratch folder for `--bg` to start.** If the start fails with "workspace not trusted", open `claude.exe` interactively once in `%USERPROFILE%\scratch` on the desktop and accept the prompt.
- **`--bg` hasn't been tested on this route.** It was only tested desktop-WSL to laptop-WSL. If it fails to start or doesn't stay up, the fallback is a `-p -n desk-win-inbox --settings "{\"crossSessionInbound\":\"accept\"}"` receiver run under `nohup ... &`. That one only lasts as long as its turn.
- **The fleet file I read was generated for desk-01, not the laptop.** I took `desk-wsl` from it but didn't check that the laptop's Windows `~/.ssh/config` defines that name. If ssh can't resolve it, use the desktop's port-2222 entry from the laptop's own copy of the fleet file.
- **Every one of these commands will ask for permission approval.** That's expected for starting Claude on another machine.
- **Don't put secrets in the prompt or messages.** They show up in the desktop's process list.
- **Apostrophes need escaping as `'\''`.** Otherwise they break the outer single quotes in these commands.

Here's the command. Run it from your lap-01 WSL shell:

```bash
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe --bg --name desk-win-inbox "You are a standing receiver on desk-01 Windows. Other sessions will message you by name. Handle each message as a task, reply to the sender when done, and stay up between messages. Stop and report if a task needs credentials or a login." < /dev/null'
```

**Why this form:**
- **Route:** It sshes from the laptop's WSL to the desktop's WSL on port 2222, then runs `claude.exe` from the Windows scratch directory. Port 22 (`desk-win`) won't work for this because the `ssh-admin` account there has no Claude sign-in. Use the Windows `ssh.exe`, because WSL holds no SSH key.
- **`--bg --name`, not `-p -n`:** A `-p` receiver stops when its single turn ends. A background session stays up and listens for messages, so other sessions can keep reaching it under the name `desk-win-inbox`.

**Before you run it:**
1. **Check that the desktop's Windows side is signed in.** The last laptop-to-desktop-Windows test found it signed out. If this returns an expired-login error, someone has to run `/login` at the desktop:
   ```bash
   /mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'hostname && cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe -p "echo ok" < /dev/null'
   ```
2. **Trust the scratch directory.** `--bg` fails with a "workspace not trusted" error unless `%USERPROFILE%\scratch` has been opened once in an interactive `claude.exe` and the trust prompt accepted.
3. **Treat this as untested.** `--bg` has only been tested on WSL. This exact Windows-side run hasn't been tried.
4. **Check the ssh alias.** The only fleet file in this session's home is the one generated for the desktop, so I took the `desk-wsl` alias from its machine table. Make sure your laptop's ssh config defines it.

**To manage it afterwards** (same hop): the `id` comes from the list command.
```bash
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe agents --json --all < /dev/null'
/mnt/c/Windows/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe desk-wsl 'cd /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/scratch && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe stop <id> && /mnt/c/Users/EvalUser/.local/bin/claude.exe rm <id>'
```

Only sessions on the desktop's Windows side can message it directly, because each side has its own account. From anywhere else, start a short session over the same connection:
```bash
claude.exe -p "SendMessage to desk-win-inbox: <text>"
```

Keep apostrophes out of the prompt text or escape them as `'\''`, and don't put secrets in it: it shows up in the desktop's process list.
